quests.instruction: Read the policy and find how much advance notice is required for remote work requests.
quests.passage: Remote Work Policy: Employees may work remotely up to three days per week with manager approval. Teams that require in-person collaboration, such as design and manufacturing, are exempt from this policy and must remain on-site full time. All remote work requests must be submitted at least one week in advance.
quests.hint: Judge which detail answers the actual question about notice, not eligibility.
quests.explanation: Requests must be submitted one week in advance; three days per week describes the remote work limit, not the notice period.
quests.targetInfo: Advance notice required for remote work requests

quests.instruction: Read the notice and find the extra requirement that applies specifically to business travelers.
quests.passage: Visa Requirements Notice: Travelers from most countries require a visa obtained in advance through the consulate. Citizens of participating countries under the visa-waiver program may instead apply for an electronic authorization online. Business travelers, regardless of nationality, must also provide a letter of invitation from their host company.
quests.hint: Judge which sentence applies to business travelers specifically, not general travelers.
quests.explanation: Business travelers must provide a letter of invitation; the visa-waiver program applies to a different group of travelers.
quests.targetInfo: Additional requirement for business travelers

quests.instruction: Read the comparison and find which model is recommended for durability.
quests.passage: Product Comparison Memo: Model A offers longer battery life but lacks water resistance. Model B is fully waterproof and includes a faster charging port, though its screen is noticeably smaller. For most users prioritizing durability, Model B is the stronger choice despite its display size.
quests.hint: Judge which model the memo actually recommends, not just which has more features listed.
quests.explanation: Model B is recommended for durability due to water resistance; Model A is discussed only for its battery life.
quests.targetInfo: Model recommended for durability

quests.instruction: Read the instructions and find how long refunds take once the item is received.
quests.passage: Return Process Instructions: Start by locating your order number on the packing slip. Log into your account and select the item you wish to return. Print the prepaid shipping label and attach it to the original box. Refunds are typically processed within five business days of the item being received at our warehouse.
quests.hint: Judge which step in the process actually answers the timing question.
quests.explanation: Refunds take five business days after the item is received; the earlier steps describe how to start the return, not the timing.
quests.targetInfo: Refund processing time

quests.instruction: Read the memo and find the new paid parental leave duration, not the meeting change.
quests.passage: Company Memo: This month's all-hands meeting has been moved to the auditorium due to expected attendance. Separately, the company is introducing a new parental leave policy offering twelve weeks of paid leave, up from eight, effective for all births and adoptions after January 1st.
quests.hint: Judge which of the two unrelated topics the question is actually about.
quests.explanation: The new leave duration is twelve weeks, up from eight; the auditorium relates to a separate, unrelated topic.
quests.targetInfo: New paid parental leave duration

quests.instruction: Read the advisory and find the specific time window of highest risk.
quests.passage: Public Health Advisory: Residents are encouraged to stay hydrated during the current heat wave. Those with existing heart or respiratory conditions should limit outdoor activity between noon and 4 p.m., the period of highest risk. Cooling centers are open citywide for anyone without air conditioning.
quests.hint: Judge which recommendation includes the specific time window asked about.
quests.explanation: The highest-risk window is noon to 4 p.m.; the hydration and cooling center advice are general recommendations.
quests.targetInfo: Highest-risk period for at-risk residents

quests.instruction: Read the comparison and find which loan option minimizes total cost for long-term owners.
quests.passage: Financing Comparison: The 36-month loan carries a lower interest rate but higher monthly payments. The 60-month loan spreads payments out further, lowering the monthly amount but increasing total interest paid over time. Buyers planning to keep the vehicle long-term often prefer the 36-month option to minimize total cost.
quests.hint: Judge which option the comparison actually recommends for long-term cost, not just which has lower monthly payments.
quests.explanation: The 36-month option minimizes total cost; the 60-month loan lowers monthly payments but costs more overall.
quests.targetInfo: Loan recommended for minimizing total cost

quests.instruction: Read the amendment and find which roles are exempt from the new, more casual dress code.
quests.passage: Employee Handbook Amendment: Section 4.1 on dress code has been updated to allow business casual attire company-wide, replacing the previous formal requirement. This change does not apply to client-facing roles, which must still follow the formal dress code during meetings.
quests.hint: Judge which group the exception actually applies to, not the general policy change.
quests.explanation: Client-facing roles are exempt and must stay formal; business casual is the new default for everyone else.
quests.targetInfo: Roles exempt from the new dress code

quests.instruction: Read the addendum and find the premium tier's guaranteed response time.
quests.passage: Service Agreement Addendum: Standard support covers issues reported during business hours, with a response time of four hours. Customers on the premium tier receive 24/7 support with a guaranteed response time of thirty minutes, regardless of when the issue is reported.
quests.hint: Judge which response time belongs to the premium tier, not the standard tier.
quests.explanation: Premium support guarantees a thirty-minute response; four hours is the standard tier's response time.
quests.targetInfo: Premium tier's guaranteed response time

quests.instruction: Read the briefing and find whether visitors must complete the forklift course.
quests.passage: Warehouse Safety Briefing: All visitors must wear a hard hat and safety vest at all times while on the floor. Forklift operators are required to complete a refresher course annually, regardless of prior certification. Visitors are not required to complete the forklift course unless they plan to operate equipment.
quests.hint: Judge which rule specifically applies to visitors, not forklift operators.
quests.explanation: Visitors are not required to take the forklift course unless operating equipment; the annual refresher applies to operators instead.
quests.targetInfo: Whether visitors must complete the forklift course

quests.instruction: Read the memo and find the daily limit for meal reimbursement.
quests.passage: Conference Travel Memo: Staff attending the conference should book flights at least three weeks in advance to secure lower fares. Hotel reservations should be made through the company's preferred booking site to qualify for reimbursement. Meals during the conference are reimbursed up to $60 per day with receipts.
quests.hint: Judge which detail actually answers the meal reimbursement question.
quests.explanation: Meals are reimbursed up to $60 per day; the flight and hotel booking advice cover separate expenses.
quests.targetInfo: Daily meal reimbursement limit

quests.instruction: Read the guide and find whether renters insurance is actually required by the lease.
quests.passage: Apartment Move-In Guide: Utilities must be transferred into the tenant's name before move-in day. A walkthrough inspection will be scheduled within 48 hours of key pickup to document any existing damage. Renters insurance, while not required by the lease, is strongly recommended by management.
quests.hint: Judge whether the guide actually requires insurance or only recommends it.
quests.explanation: Renters insurance is not required by the lease, only strongly recommended; the 48-hour window applies to the walkthrough instead.
quests.targetInfo: Whether renters insurance is required

quests.instruction: Read the terms and find how many personal devices a single license covers.
quests.passage: Software License Terms: A single license permits installation on up to two personal devices. Commercial use requires a separate business license, purchased at a different rate. Sharing login credentials with anyone outside your household violates the terms of this agreement.
quests.hint: Judge which sentence actually answers the device-count question, not the commercial-use rule.
quests.explanation: A single license covers two personal devices; commercial use requires an entirely separate license.
quests.targetInfo: Number of devices a single license covers

quests.instruction: Read the terms and find what elite members get access to beyond the standard tier.
quests.passage: Gym Membership Terms: Standard members have access to the main workout floor and locker rooms only. Members on the elite tier gain additional access to the pool, sauna, and group fitness classes at no extra charge. All memberships require a thirty-day written notice to cancel.
quests.targetItem: pool, sauna, and group fitness classes
options: pool, sauna, and group fitness classes
quests.correctAnswer: pool, sauna, and group fitness classes
quests.hint: Judge which access applies to the elite tier specifically, not the standard tier.
quests.explanation: Elite members get the pool, sauna, and group fitness classes; standard members are limited to the floor and locker rooms.
quests.targetInfo: Additional access for elite members

quests.instruction: Read the notice and find the declaration rule that applies to items intended for resale.
quests.passage: Import Regulations Notice: Personal items valued under $800 generally do not require a customs declaration. Items intended for resale must be declared regardless of value. Travelers bringing food products should check restrictions in advance, as many fresh items are prohibited entirely.
quests.hint: Judge which rule applies specifically to resale items, not personal items.
quests.explanation: Resale items must be declared regardless of value; the $800 threshold applies only to personal items.
quests.targetInfo: Declaration rule for resale items

quests.instruction: Read the policy and find the consequence for permit holders who park on Level 1 without authorization.
quests.passage: Parking Garage Policy: Monthly permit holders may park in any unreserved spot on levels 2 through 5. Level 1 is reserved exclusively for visitors and deliveries. Permit holders who park on Level 1 without authorization may have their vehicle towed at their own expense.
quests.hint: Judge which sentence actually describes the consequence, not just the parking zones.
quests.explanation: Unauthorized Level 1 parking can result in towing at the owner's expense; levels 2 through 5 are where permit holders normally park.
quests.targetInfo: Consequence for unauthorized Level 1 parking

quests.instruction: Read the update and find the correct way teachers should now request technical support.
quests.passage: Classroom Technology Update: All classrooms have been equipped with new projectors this semester. Teachers who need technical support should submit a ticket through the IT portal rather than calling the help desk directly, as phone lines are being phased out. Support requests are typically resolved within one business day.
quests.hint: Judge which method is actually correct now, not the outdated one being phased out.
quests.explanation: Teachers should use the IT portal; the help desk phone line is being phased out.
quests.targetInfo: Correct way to request technical support

quests.instruction: Read the policy and find how far in advance large parties must reserve.
quests.passage: Restaurant Reservation Policy: Parties of six or fewer can be seated without a reservation, subject to availability. Parties of seven or more must reserve at least 24 hours in advance and provide a credit card to hold the table. A cancellation fee applies for no-shows on reserved tables.
quests.hint: Judge which rule applies to large parties specifically, not small ones.
quests.explanation: Parties of seven or more need 24 hours notice; parties of six or fewer can walk in without a reservation.
quests.targetInfo: Advance notice required for large parties

quests.instruction: Read the comparison and find the feature that comes only with the pro tier.
quests.passage: Cloud Storage Plan Comparison: The free tier includes 5GB of storage with ads. The plus tier removes ads and increases storage to 100GB for a monthly fee. The pro tier, aimed at businesses, includes 2TB of storage plus priority customer support.
quests.hint: Judge which feature is exclusive to the pro tier, not shared with the others.
quests.explanation: Priority support comes only with the pro tier; 5GB and 100GB describe storage on the free and plus tiers.
quests.targetInfo: Feature exclusive to the pro tier

quests.instruction: Read the instructions and find whether accidental damage is covered under the standard warranty.
quests.passage: Warranty Claim Instructions: Before filing a claim, check that your product is still within the coverage period listed on your receipt. Claims for accidental damage are not covered under the standard warranty and require separate accidental damage protection. Approved claims are typically resolved within ten business days.
quests.hint: Judge whether the standard warranty actually includes accidental damage.
quests.explanation: Accidental damage is not covered under the standard warranty; a separate protection plan is required for that.
quests.targetInfo: Whether accidental damage is covered under the standard warranty

quests.instruction: Read the update and find how the fare increase affects reduced-fare riders.
quests.passage: Public Transit Fare Update: Standard fares will increase by 25 cents starting next month. Riders using the reduced-fare program for seniors and students will not see any change in their current rate. Monthly passes will also remain at their current price through the end of the year.
quests.hint: Judge which group of riders is actually unaffected by the increase.
quests.explanation: Reduced-fare riders will not see any change; the 25-cent increase applies only to standard fares.
quests.targetInfo: Effect of the fare increase on reduced-fare riders

quests.instruction: Read the guide and find where requests for specialty equipment must be submitted.
quests.passage: Office Supply Ordering Guide: Standard supplies like paper and pens can be ordered directly through the online portal without approval. Orders over $200 require manager sign-off before processing. Specialty equipment requests must go through the procurement department instead of the standard portal.
quests.hint: Judge which channel applies to specialty equipment, not standard supplies.
quests.explanation: Specialty equipment goes through procurement; the online portal is only for standard supplies.
quests.targetInfo: Where specialty equipment requests must go

quests.instruction: Read the rules and find what happens if a bike isn't returned within 24 hours.
quests.passage: Bike Share Program Rules: Rides under 30 minutes are included in the base membership at no extra charge. Rides between 30 and 60 minutes incur a $2 fee. Members who fail to return a bike within 24 hours are charged the full replacement cost of the bike.
quests.hint: Judge which rule applies to bikes not returned at all, not just longer rides.
quests.explanation: Bikes not returned within 24 hours incur the full replacement cost; the $2 fee applies only to longer rides, not missing bikes.
quests.targetInfo: Charge for not returning a bike within 24 hours

quests.instruction: Read the policy and find the refund rule for withdrawals after week four.
quests.passage: Course Withdrawal Policy: Students may withdraw from a course with a full refund during the first two weeks of the semester. Withdrawals during weeks three and four receive a 50 percent refund. No refunds are issued for withdrawals after week four.
quests.hint: Judge which rule applies to the latest withdrawal period, not the earlier ones.
quests.explanation: After week four, no refunds are issued; full and 50 percent refunds apply only to earlier withdrawal periods.
quests.targetInfo: Refund policy after week four

quests.instruction: Read the notice and find whether the company sells collected data to third parties.
quests.passage: Data Privacy Notice: We collect basic usage data to improve our services, such as which features are used most often. This data is never sold to third parties. Users may request a full copy of their collected data or ask for it to be deleted at any time through account settings.
quests.hint: Judge which sentence directly answers whether data is sold.
quests.explanation: Data is never sold to third parties; usage data collection and account settings are separate details.
quests.targetInfo: Whether collected data is sold to third parties

quests.instruction: Read the guidelines and find what craft and retail vendors must submit in place of a health permit.
quests.passage: Event Vendor Guidelines: Food vendors must submit health permits at least two weeks before the event. Craft and retail vendors are not required to submit health permits but must provide proof of liability insurance instead. All vendors must be set up and ready by 8 a.m. on the event day.
quests.hint: Judge which requirement applies to craft and retail vendors, not food vendors.
quests.explanation: Craft and retail vendors need liability insurance instead of a health permit, which is required only for food vendors.
quests.targetInfo: What craft and retail vendors must submit instead of a health permit

quests.instruction: Read the guide and find how long to hold the pairing button if the remote fails to connect.
quests.passage: Streaming Device Setup Guide: Connect the device to your TV using the included HDMI cable. Once powered on, follow the on-screen prompts to connect to your home Wi-Fi network. If the remote fails to pair automatically, hold the pairing button for ten seconds to reset the connection.
quests.hint: Judge which step applies only when the automatic pairing fails.
quests.explanation: Holding the button for ten seconds resets pairing if it fails; the earlier steps describe normal setup.
quests.targetInfo: How long to hold the pairing button if it fails to connect

quests.instruction: Read the policy and find whether business class on long international flights requires separate approval.
quests.passage: Corporate Travel Policy Update: Economy class remains standard for domestic flights under five hours. Flights longer than five hours qualify for premium economy upgrades, subject to manager approval. International flights over ten hours qualify for business class without requiring separate approval.
quests.hint: Judge which flight category does not need manager approval, unlike the others.
quests.explanation: Long international flights get business class without separate approval; premium economy upgrades still need manager approval.
quests.targetInfo: Approval requirement for long international flights

quests.instruction: Read the notice and find the maximum percentage the company will match.
quests.passage: Retirement Plan Enrollment Notice: New employees are automatically enrolled in the retirement plan at a 3 percent contribution rate unless they opt out within thirty days. Employees may increase their contribution rate at any time through the online portal. The company matches contributions up to 4 percent.
quests.hint: Judge which figure is the company's match, not the default enrollment rate.
quests.explanation: The company matches up to 4 percent; 3 percent is only the default automatic contribution rate.
quests.targetInfo: Maximum company match

quests.instruction: Read the policy and find what groups larger than thirty must arrange.
quests.passage: Museum Group Tour Policy: Groups of ten or fewer may book a tour with 48 hours notice. Groups of eleven to thirty require one week's notice and a nonrefundable deposit. Groups larger than thirty must contact the events office directly to arrange a custom itinerary.
quests.hint: Judge which rule applies to the largest group size, not the smaller ones.
quests.explanation: Groups larger than thirty arrange a custom itinerary through the events office; the other notice periods apply to smaller groups.
quests.targetInfo: What large groups must arrange through the events office
